title: Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin
subtitle: Two visitors to Dracula's castle
summary: Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin is Konami's Nintendo DS action role-playing game set in Europe during the Second World War. body: Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin is Konami's Nintendo DS action role-playing game set in Europe during the Second World War. Jonathan Morris and Charlotte Aulin investigate a castle whose paintings lead into other locations. Jonathan brings physical combat skills, while Charlotte specialises in magic. Their partnership gives the adventure two distinct ways to approach an enemy or obstacle. The castle remains the centre of an interconnected journey, but the paintings allow it to open onto environments that are visually and geographically different from its own rooms.

The player can switch between Jonathan and Charlotte or call the other character into action as a partner. Their different abilities make the choice useful beyond the appearance of the next attack. Combined techniques encourage the pair to work together, while particular obstacles require their skills in the right arrangement. Equipment and experience continue to support the role-playing progression. Instead of replacing one protagonist with another for an entire chapter, Portrait of Ruin makes their relationship available as an ordinary decision throughout movement, exploration and fighting.

The paintings interrupt the castle's familiar architecture with places such as an Egyptian desert and a town inspired by London. Entering one changes the setting without abandoning the larger investigation. Returning to the castle then restores a shared point of reference for the journey. The game also introduces a separate cooperative mode through online play, extending the idea of a pair beyond its story characters. Its most distinctive contribution remains the accessible partnership: two complementary people can occupy the centre of a Castlevania adventure at once.
